entries.description: callGoJSON returns parsed.result as T without verifying result is non-null. When Go serializes a nil interface{} to JSON null, parsed.result will be null at runtime but the GoOutput<T> type declares result as optional (T | undefined), not (T | null). With exactOptionalPropertyTypes and strictNullChecks enabled, null would fail type checking but the unsafe cast bypasses this. If a Go command returns ok:true with a nil result, the caller receives null instead of a meaningful T, causing downstream TypeError when accessing properties.
entries.suggestion: Add a runtime guard after line 135: if (parsed.result === undefined || parsed.result === null) throw new Error(...). Or change GoOutput.result to include null in the union.

entries.description: claims.status is cast as TerminalWorkerStatus without validation. If a real worker returns a status string not in the TerminalWorkerStatus union (e.g. running, pending, cancelled), the unsafe cast silently passes it through. The Go finalizer accepts only specific terminal statuses and would reject the build. The claims parser validates that status is a non-empty string but does not validate it is a recognized terminal value.
entries.suggestion: Add runtime validation in dispatchRealWorker: if (!TERMINAL_WORKER_STATUSES.has(claims.status)) { claims.status = "failed" } or throw an error.

entries.description: Non-null assertion on waveMap.get(waveNum) in dispatchWaves. The code iterates over keys from the same map, so the get should always succeed. However, if the map were modified concurrently (e.g. by a spawned child wave modifying shared state), this could throw TypeError. Currently single-threaded so no real risk.
entries.suggestion: Safe as-is for single-threaded execution. If concurrency is ever added, replace with a guard.

entries.description: Non-null assertion on child.stdout. The spawn call at line 122 uses stdio:["ignore","pipe","pipe"], so stdout should always be a Readable stream. However, if the spawn fails silently or stdio is misconfigured, child.stdout could be null. The ! assertion bypasses this check.
entries.suggestion: Add a guard: if (!child.stdout) throw new Error("event-bridge: subprocess stdout not available")

entries.description: Non-null assertion waves[key]!.push(dispatch). The preceding if (!waves[key]) initializes it, so this is safe. The assertion is redundant but harmless.
entries.suggestion: Replace with (waves[key] ?? []).push(dispatch) or just remove the ! since the if-guard makes it provably non-null.

entries.description: planManifest[goal] is cast as string after typeof check. This is a valid pattern -- the typeof guard proves it is a string at runtime, and the cast satisfies TypeScript after indexing into Record<string,unknown>. Safe.
entries.suggestion: No change needed.

entries.description: Worker handoff is cast as WorkerHandoff without deep validation. If a worker returns a handoff object with unexpected fields or wrong types, the cast silently passes. This is acceptable because WorkerHandoff uses an index signature [key:string]:unknown which allows arbitrary fields.
entries.suggestion: No change needed -- the index signature makes this inherently flexible.

entries.description: Test "lifecycle handles QueenOrchestrator failure gracefully" asserts result.success is true even though the Queen returned an error. The lifecycle catches Queen errors and logs them (line 494) but still reports success because the build-finalizer and continue-finalizer steps succeeded with mock workers. This is correct behavior -- the Queen error is informational, not fatal. The test name is slightly misleading.
entries.suggestion: Consider renaming test to "lifecycle logs Queen error but continues through finalizers".

entries.description: The seen set LRU eviction at line 153-160 correctly handles memory growth when streaming events for extended periods. The simple half-clear strategy prevents unbounded Set growth.
entries.suggestion: None needed.

entries.description: The ok/error check at line 130 correctly handles both stdout error envelopes and stderr error envelopes. The sanitizeBridgeMessage function redacts secrets before error propagation.
entries.suggestion: None needed.

entries.description: The finally block at line 639-644 correctly ensures the dashboard is always stopped even on error, preventing terminal state corruption. The dashboard variable is nulled after stop to prevent double-stop.
entries.suggestion: None needed.

entries.description: assertNoWriteToData correctly normalizes path separators and checks against GO_OWNED_PATHS. The assertNoDirectDataWrites in go-bridge.ts additionally resolves .. traversal segments.
entries.suggestion: None needed.

entries.description: Legacy flat wrapper .claude/commands/ant-build.md uses `aether host build $ARGUMENTS` without --dry-run. The updated nested wrappers at .claude/commands/ant/build.md and .opencode/commands/ant/build.md correctly use `aether host build --dry-run`, but this legacy file still triggers the TS host dispatched path which spawns workers in parallel with the wrapper spawning, causing the exact double-dispatch problem that was fixed. The Go test TestBuildWrapperCeremonyContract only validates the nested paths, not this legacy file.
entries.suggestion: Either update .claude/commands/ant-build.md to use --dry-run and match the nested wrappers, or remove the legacy file entirely since Claude Code resolves /ant-build to .claude/commands/ant/build.md via subdirectory resolution.

entries.description: Legacy flat wrapper .claude/commands/ant-continue.md uses `aether host continue --classic-ceremony $ARGUMENTS` without --dry-run for the heavy review path. The updated nested wrappers correctly use `aether host continue --dry-run --classic-ceremony`, but this legacy file triggers the TS host dispatched path, causing double-dispatch of review workers. This file is also missing the Ownership Split section and the guardrail about using --dry-run.
entries.suggestion: Update .claude/commands/ant-continue.md to use --dry-run and match the nested wrappers, or remove the legacy file.

entries.description: The Codex skill aether-colony-build-cycle uses `aether host build <phase>` (line 156) and `aether host continue --classic-ceremony <args>` (line 208) without --dry-run. Since Codex is a secondary platform with best-effort support, the double-dispatch risk is lower, but if a Codex user triggers build or heavy continue, they will experience the same double-dispatch problem that was fixed for Claude/OpenCode.
entries.suggestion: Update the Codex skill to use `aether host build --dry-run <phase>` and `aether host continue --dry-run --classic-ceremony <args>` to match the wrapper-host contract.

entries.description: The patterns/ and learnings/ directories exist at the repo root (untracked per git ls-files). These contain 12 markdown files that appear to be Keeper-generated analysis artifacts. They are not in .aether/ and could clutter the repo root, potentially confusing tooling or users. The learnings/ directory contains a double-dispatch preservation risk note that suggests these were created during this investigation phase.
entries.suggestion: Move patterns/ and learnings/ into .aether/data/ or remove them if they were temporary analysis artifacts.

entries.description: The dry-run path in runDryRunDispatchedCommand gracefully handles empty/null manifests by falling back to empty dispatches array (line 490-495) and still outputs valid JSON with ok:true and dry_run:true. However, it does not validate that the manifest contains dispatch_manifest or continue_manifest fields specifically -- if Go returns an unexpected JSON shape, the dry-run output may have an empty manifest field but the wrapper will still receive ok:true.
entries.suggestion: Consider adding a warning to stderr when the manifest has no recognizable dispatch structure in dry-run mode, so the wrapper has a signal to detect missing data.

entries.description: The go-bridge properly handles malformed JSON from Go (line 121-124: throws descriptive error) and Go error envelopes (line 130-133: throws with sanitized message). However, the wrapper markdown has no explicit instructions for handling JSON parse failures from the TS host. If `aether host build --dry-run` outputs broken JSON (e.g., Go crash, encoding issue), the wrapper has no documented recovery path.
entries.suggestion: Add a wrapper guardrail for handling TS host JSON parse failures: if the host output is not valid JSON, surface the error and suggest running `aether status` to check colony state.

entries.description: The --dry-run flag is well-supported in the TS host: parsed at line 165, documented at line 274, and has three code paths: dispatched commands (line 1074), go-json commands (line 1113), and oracle-lifecycle (line 1125). Each path returns {ok:true, dry_run:true, manifest:...} JSON. The dry-run path calls the same Go --plan-only commands as the dispatched path but stops before spawning workers. This is correctly implemented.
entries.suggestion: No action needed.

entries.description: Claude and OpenCode build.md wrappers are byte-identical (diff produced no output). Continue.md wrappers are also byte-identical. Cross-platform drift guard is working correctly for the updated files.
entries.suggestion: No action needed.
